varianceWarning: These are MARGINAL shares: the variance each factor explains alone. They are NOT additive and do NOT partition total variance. User and item effects are crossed and unbalanced, so their sums of squares share variance — verified on complete Gift_Cards data where the marginals sum to 105.62%, which is impossible for an orthogonal decomposition. Do not compute a residual from these, and do not read them as 'X% is the product, Y% is the rater'.
notes: The `Unknown` category is excluded, matching Phase 1. It is 11% of ratings but 42% of users (23.1M of 54.51M) — disproportionately one-and-done reviewers, so excluding it biases every user-grain statistic toward the prolific end. THE DIRECTION IS NOW QUANTIFIED, not just asserted: user_one_and_done.csv shows mean rating rising monotonically with reviewer activity across all 507.7M reviews — 3.8126 stars for users with one review, 4.2573 for users with ten or more. Sparse reviewers rate LOWER, and `Unknown` is disproportionately sparse, so excluding it biases published mean ratings UPWARD. Treat every mean rating here as an upper bound on the all-categories figure. Note also that `Unknown` IS present in this repo's categories.txt; it is absent from published output because its Phase 1 job produced no results, not because it was never enumerated.

Tiers 2 and 3 are derived from a 64-bucket hash partitioning of the extract. Per-bucket statistics are combined by summing sufficient statistics, so Ginis, Lorenz curves and weighted means are exact rather than averaged — averaging per-bucket Ginis would not give the Gini of the union.

Measure 22 ships as variance_marginal_shares.csv and is NOT a variance decomposition. User identity explains 30.24% of rating variance and item identity 19.34%, as MARGINAL shares that do not sum to 100% and do not partition. See variance_marginal_shares_detail.

notPublished.measure: plan §4 item 9 — items with zero reviews
notPublished.reason: Unanswerable from this corpus. Exactly 0 items have rating_number=0, across all 35,003,183 items in all 33 categories. raw_meta_* contains only items that appear in the reviews split, so the denominator the measure needs — all listed products, reviewed or not — is absent. Publishing 0% everywhere would state a fact about Amazon that is actually an artifact of how the dataset was built.

notPublished.measure: plan §4 item 14 — page rating vs computed rating
notPublished.reason: Deferred, not abandoned. Computing it during the Tier 1 metadata scan required a second full read of the 245.5GB review corpus for per-item rating means, nearly doubling that tier's network cost for one comparison. Once Pass 1's by_item extract exists the same comparison is a local join. The SQL is already written in process_metadata_job.py:page_vs_computed_rating.
